hints: Look carefully at the x-axis in each graph. Which variable, enzyme or substrate concentration, levels off to a plateau when active sites become saturated?
Remember what the two labels mean: Vmax is a rate on the y-axis, while Km is the substrate concentration on the x-axis that gives exactly half of Vmax.
walkthrough:
**Check the correct x-axis variable**

Think about saturation. As you add more substrate, all enzyme active sites eventually fill up, so rate plateaus.

Adding more enzyme does not plateau in this way, rate keeps rising linearly if substrate is in excess. So the x-axis must be concentration of substrate, which rules out A and D.

**Place Vmax and Km correctly**

Vmax is the maximum rate of reaction, so it is a horizontal line from the plateau to the y-axis.

$$V \text{ at } K_m = \frac{V_{max}}{2}$$
Km is defined as the substrate concentration that gives half Vmax, so Km must be marked on the x-axis.

**Pick the matching graph**

Only graph B has substrate on the x-axis, Vmax on the y-axis, and Km on the x-axis at half Vmax.

That combination is exactly the Michaelis-Menten definition, so B is correct.

options.A: Wrong x-axis and wrong Km label. Km is never an enzyme concentration or a rate, and rate vs enzyme does not plateau like this.
options.B: Correct. X-axis is substrate concentration, Vmax is the plateau rate on the y-axis, and Km is the substrate concentration giving half Vmax on the x-axis.
options.C: X-axis is correct, but Km is wrongly shown on the y-axis. Km is a substrate concentration, so it must be on the x-axis.
options.D: Km and Vmax positions look right, but the x-axis is wrong. This saturation curve is only obtained by varying substrate concentration, not enzyme concentration.
